memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Therefore I say to the Israelites, "None of you may eat blood, nor may any foreigner residing among you eat blood."'" - Lev 17:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Given what verse 11 has just said, this prohibition makes sense. Blood represents life, and life belongs to God. To consume it casually would be to treat as ordinary what God had set apart for atonement.

This particular line held longer than most. When the early church wrestled with how Gentile believers should live, the Jerusalem Council concluded that they should not be burdened with the whole law — and then added a short list, including abstaining from blood (Acts 15:28-29).

Christians have understood that decision in different ways ever since, and sincere believers land in different places. What matters for us is the principle underneath it: the council was asking how to live together across deep cultural differences without either side despising the other.

That is Paul's great theme in Romans 14. Accept the one whose faith is weak, without quarrelling over disputable matters (Rom 14:1). Do not let what you eat destroy someone for whom Christ died.

Some things are non-negotiable — the person and work of Christ, the truth of the gospel. Others are matters where believers may differ. Wisdom is knowing which is which, and love is refusing to divide over the second kind.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you distinguish between core truths and disputable matters?
2. Where have you made a secondary issue into a test of fellowship?
3. How can you honour a believer who sees a disputable matter differently?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me clarity to hold firmly to what is essential and grace to hold loosely what is not. Keep me from dividing over what should never divide Your people. Amen.
